## Backup Strategy Overview

**Server:** [Server Name / IP]
**Primary World:** [world name]
**Backup Location (Local):** `/backups/`
**Backup Location (Off-site):** [S3 / GCS / R2 / Wasabi / SFTP / Rsync target]
**Retention Policy:** Daily: 30 days | Weekly: 12 weeks | Monthly: 12 months | Yearly: 3 years
**Encryption:** [AES-256 / GPG / None — recommend AES-256 for off-site]

---

## What to Back Up

### Critical (Every Backup)
- [ ] World folders (`world/`, `world_nether/`, `world_the_end/`, custom worlds)
- [ ] `plugins/` (all JARs + config folders)
- [ ] `server.properties`
- [ ] `paper.yml` / `spigot.yml` / `bukkit.yml` / `purpur.yml` / `folia.yml`
- [ ] `config.yml` for each plugin
- [ ] `permissions.yml` / `bukkit.yml` / `commands.yml`
- [ ] Database dumps (MySQL/MariaDB/PostgreSQL)
- [ ] `banned-players.json`, `banned-ips.json`, `ops.json`, `whitelist.json`
- [ ] `usercache.json`, `server-icon.png`

### Important (Weekly)
- [ ] Logs (`logs/` — last 7 days)
- [ ] Plugin data folders (dynmap tiles, CoreProtect databases, etc.)
- [ ] Mods folder (if Forge/Fabric/NeoForge)
- [ ] Resource packs / datapacks
- [ ] Start scripts / systemd service files
- [ ] Java version / JVM flags documentation

### Configuration (Monthly / On Change)
- [ ] OS configuration (firewall, SSH, sysctl)
- [ ] Docker compose / container definitions
- [ ] Monitoring/alerting configs (Prometheus, Grafana, etc.)
- [ ] DNS records documentation
- [ ] SSL certificates (Let's Encrypt / custom)

## Backup Schedule

### Automated (Cron / systemd timer / Backup Plugin)

| Frequency | Time (UTC) | Scope | Destination | Retention |
|-----------|------------|-------|-------------|-----------|
| Every 6h | 00:00, 06:00, 12:00, 18:00 | Incremental (world + plugins) | Local + Off-site | 30 days |
| Daily | 03:00 | Full (all critical) | Local + Off-site | 30 days |
| Weekly | Sun 04:00 | Full + important | Off-site | 12 weeks |
| Monthly | 1st 05:00 | Complete (everything) | Off-site (cold storage) | 3 years |

### Pre-Change Backups (Manual Trigger)
- [ ] Before server software update
- [ ] Before major plugin update
- [ ] Before config overhaul
- [ ] Before world edit operations
- [ ] Before map reset / new world

## Backup Methods

### Method 1: Rsync + Tar (Linux)
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# /usr/local/bin/mc-backup.sh
DATE=$(date +%F-%H%M)
DEST="/backups/minecraft/$DATE"
mkdir -p "$DEST"

# Stop server gracefully (optional for crash-consistent)
# systemctl stop minecraft

# Backup worlds
tar -czf "$DEST/worlds.tar.gz" -C /opt/minecraft world world_nether world_the_end

# Backup plugins & configs
tar -czf "$DEST/plugins.tar.gz" -C /opt/minecraft plugins

# Backup configs
tar -czf "$DEST/configs.tar.gz" -C /opt/minecraft server.properties paper.yml spigot.yml bukkit.yml

# Database
mysqldump -u backup_user -p"$DB_PASS" minecraft | gzip > "$DEST/database.sql.gz"

# Encrypt (optional)
# gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256 "$DEST"/*.tar.gz

# Upload to off-site
rclone copy "$DEST" remote:minecraft-backups/$DATE

# Cleanup local > 30 days
find /backups/minecraft -type d -mtime +30 -exec rm -rf {} \;

# Restart server
# systemctl start minecraft
```

### Method 2: Plugin-Based (Server-Side)
- **CoreProtect:** Built-in backup command
- **ServerRestorer:** Custom backup/restore
- **Backup plugins:** Backup, SimpleBackup, etc.
- **Pros:** No downtime, incremental
- **Cons:** May miss files, plugin-dependent

### Method 3: Cloud Provider Snapshots (VPS)
- AWS/Azure/GCP/DigitalOcean: Disk snapshots
- Pros: Full system state, fast restore
- Cons: Cost, not granular, provider lock-in

### Method 4: Container/Volume Backup (Docker)
```bash
docker run --rm -v minecraft_data:/data -v /backups:/backup alpine \
  tar czf /backup/minecraft-$(date +%F).tar.gz -C /data .
```

## Recovery Procedures

### Scenario 1: Single File Corruption (config.yml)
1. Identify corrupted file
2. Locate latest clean backup: `ls -la /backups/minecraft/ | tail -20`
3. Extract: `tar -xzf /backups/minecraft/2024-01-15-0300/configs.tar.gz -C /tmp`
4. Copy: `cp /tmp/server.properties /opt/minecraft/`
5. Restart: `systemctl restart minecraft`

### Scenario 2: World Corruption / Grief Recovery
1. Stop server: `systemctl stop minecraft`
2. Find last good backup (check logs for corruption time)
3. Extract world: `tar -xzf /backups/minecraft/2024-01-15-0300/worlds.tar.gz -C /tmp`
4. Replace: `rm -rf /opt/minecraft/world && mv /tmp/world /opt/minecraft/`
5. Start: `systemctl start minecraft`
6. Verify: Check console for errors, test spawn area

### Scenario 3: Complete Server Loss (Hardware Failure)
1. Provision new server (same OS, Java version)
2. Install dependencies: `apt install openjdk-21-jre-headless rclone`
3. Restore off-site backup:
   ```bash
   rclone copy remote:minecraft-backups/2024-01-15-0300 /tmp/restore
   ```
4. Extract all archives to `/opt/minecraft/`
5. Restore database:
   ```bash
   gunzip -c /tmp/restore/database.sql.gz | mysql -u root -p minecraft
   ```
6. Recreate systemd service / start script
7. Test startup: `java -jar paper.jar --nogui`
8. Update DNS / firewall
9. Announce to community

### Scenario 4: Plugin/Config Update Gone Wrong
1. Stop server
2. Restore `plugins/` and configs from pre-update backup
3. Start server
4. Test functionality
5. Re-apply update carefully

### Scenario 5: Database Corruption
1. Stop server
2. Restore latest SQL dump:
   ```bash
   gunzip -c /backups/minecraft/latest/database.sql.gz | mysql -u root -p minecraft
   ```
3. If using SQLite: Replace `.db` file from backup
4. Start server
5. Verify player data (inventory, permissions, economy)

---

## Testing & Verification

### Monthly (Required)
- [ ] Restore single config file from backup
- [ ] Verify backup integrity (checksums match)
- [ ] Test off-site accessibility (download test file)
- [ ] Verify encryption/decryption works

### Quarterly (Required)
- [ ] **Full disaster recovery drill:**
  - [ ] Spin up test server (separate VPS/local VM)
  - [ ] Restore latest full backup
  - [ ] Verify server starts cleanly
  - [ ] Test player join, commands, world integrity
  - [ ] Document time-to-recovery (RTO)
  - [ ] Document data loss (RPO)
- [ ] Review and update this checklist

### Annually
- [ ] Test restore from oldest retained backup
- [ ] Verify off-site provider SLA
- [ ] Review backup costs vs. risk
- [ ] Update recovery contacts

## Monitoring & Alerts

- [ ] Backup success/failure alerts (Discord/email/PagerDuty)
- [ ] Disk space alerts (> 80% on backup volume)
- [ ] Off-site sync lag alerts
- [ ] Backup size anomaly alerts (sudden drop = incomplete)
- [ ] Monthly backup report (size, duration, success rate)

## Quick Reference Card

**Local Backups:** `/backups/minecraft/`
**Off-site:** `rclone remote:minecraft-backups/`
**Latest Full:** `ls -td /backups/minecraft/*/ | head -1`
**Restore Command:** `tar -xzf <backup.tar.gz> -C /opt/minecraft/`
**DB Restore:** `gunzip -c <dump.sql.gz> | mysql -u root -p dbname`
**RTO Target:** < 2 hours | **RPO Target:** < 6 hours
